executiveSummary: GM0268's 2025 identity, contained reference point, 189,007-resident control, forty-four neighbourhoods, Lent and Nijmegen BAG places, two BRT woonkernen, five rail stations and six logical road-border links are internally coherent; all ten canonical presets also execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Nijmegen's direct flood geography is divided by the Waal, the defended Waalsprong/Lent north bank, the higher urban terrain south and east of the river, local low points and sewers, the Waalfront/Honig partly buitendijkse transition, Spiegelwaal, Maas-Waalkanaal and Sluis Weurt. Waterschap records show continuing defence projects under post-2017 norms; they are lifecycle evidence, not a live protection guarantee or breach. The simulator instead reports an unselected municipality-wide river depth of 3.300457 at both T+24 and T+72, 84,443 rising to 91,643 affected residents, and 1,927,869 rising to 7,388,603 person-hours. Even elevated eastern neighbourhood Kwakkenberg receives 635 affected residents at T+24. Rijkswaterstaat's dated Waal forecast supplies point water levels only through T+24 for Nijmegen and no T+48/T+72 point, never an inundation footprint. Pluvial T+24 likewise reports depth 0.351353 and 12,333 affected after rainfall is zero without the municipal stress-test, AHN, sewer, gully, ditch, pump, receiving-water or recession state. Nine active hazard/component families reuse one seeded forty-four-neighbourhood surface. A controlled wildfire source in Kwakkenberg produces city flame 0.513013, smoke 0.566285 and 47,436 affected residents, but Kwakkenberg itself has only 378 affected and ranks thirty-sixth by absolute affected population while remote Lent ranks first. Public context contains sixty partial water assets, three local Waterinfo observations, four Waal forecasts through T+24, two indicative air stations, 239 antenna sites, 129 education locations and two 24/7 emergency hospitals. These records do not publish live connectivity, capacity, backup, staffing, acceptance, outage or restoration. The six road links also omit explicit state for Waal/Spiegelwaal and Maas-Waalkanaal crossings; two A73 series entries use inconsistent physical-corridor identifiers and N326 has none. The regional care risk profile explicitly records unknown staff reachability, access, buffers, chain responsibilities and emergency capacity in flood, water, power and ICT scenarios. Exact first-72-hour service and recovery percentages must therefore remain visibly synthetic or Unknown until an event-specific hydraulic/fire/weather/cyber footprint, valid-time lifeline state and accountable action/resource ledger are bound; missing public data is never zero, safe, open or recovered.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0268 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality and regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0268 as Nijmegen in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Gelderland-Zuid, with 189,007 residents, density 3,579/km², 16.9% aged 65 or older and 57,902 one-person households. The reference point [5.833273901272997,51.83964909111373] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary.

Forty-four neighbourhoods in nine districts sum to 189,020 residents, thirteen above the municipal control (+0.007%); published households total 104,375 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 32,010. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 189,007 without rewriting observations.

Lent and Nijmegen are the two BAG places and both retained centres lie inside the generalized boundary. The two BRT features are woonkernen, not independent population controls, evacuation sites or shelters.

District-heating and public-charging fields are null in all 44 neighbourhoods; eleven other statistics have one to four null neighbourhood rows. Null remains scoped NoData, not numeric zero or service absence.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Klimaatadaptatiestrategie Nijmegen and current water-nuisance guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal page inspected 3 September 2026; linked Klimaatadaptatiestrategie considered by the council in December 2023; planning/context evidence; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The municipality distinguishes heat, drought, extreme rainfall, hail and storm and describes green roofs/facades, wadis, storage, trees and disconnecting rainwater pipes as adaptation measures. These are planning measures, not an incident-time state.

The strategy explicitly seeks to prevent building/infrastructure damage during heavy rainfall, maintain vital functions and reduce consequences in Waal-overflow and buitendijkse areas. It therefore treats mechanisms and locations separately rather than as one city-wide depth.

Current water-nuisance guidance distinguishes street rainfall, sewer/ditch, basement and groundwater pathways and reports groundwater nuisance in western Nijmegen since late 2023. Blocked gullies, sewer capacity and low street location are named causes.
The page and strategy do not publish a selected storm, sewer state, local depth forecast, intervention completion, pump availability or neighbourhood T+72 recovery.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Waalfront, Sprok–Sterreschans–Heteren and Spiegelwaal flood-system context
evidenceSources.edition: Current authority project pages inspected 3 September 2026; Room for the River works 2013–2015 and current dike-project lifecycle; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: At Waalfront the authority is modifying about one kilometre of water barrier between the rail bridge and De Oversteek. New development incorporates water-retaining functions and part of the Honig site becomes buitendijks; completed and pending sections remain distinct.

Waterschap states that parts of the dike from Sprok/Lent toward Sterreschans and Heteren require strengthening under the risk-based standards introduced in 2017. The earlier Nijmegen Room for the River intervention does not eliminate the later assessment need.

Rijkswaterstaat describes the Spiegelwaal as connected by culverts and flowing when high Waal water crosses its threshold. Water level, threshold, dike/barrier state and terrain determine pathways; none is established by a municipality scalar.
Project completion, design intent and assessment are lifecycle/context evidence, not a live no-failure guarantee, breach selection, inundation footprint, arrival time or all-clear.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Temporary drought pumps for Waalsprong water levels
evidenceSources.edition: Published 7 August 2026; dated operational context for exceptional low Rhine/Waal levels; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The water board installed three temporary pumps in Waalsprong because exceptionally low Rhine and Waal levels meant fixed pumps would soon be unable to supply ponds in Lent and Oosterhout.

The action aimed to avoid fish mortality and damage to clay layers; earlier high-river seepage water had been retained in seasonal storage. This proves coupled drought, river, storage and pump mechanisms.
This dated action is not a generic future scenario input and must not silently persist beyond its validity. Pump location, status, power, flow, stock and crew availability need current confirmation.
An absent later update is Unknown, not proof that pumps remain active, that levels are normal, or that T+72 demand can be met.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Zorgrisicoprofiel 2024 Gelderland-Zuid
evidenceSources.edition: Final regional care-risk profile adopted 25 April 2024; planning/scenario evidence; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The profile prioritises river high water, contaminated drinking water, electricity outage, ICT/telecom outage and a toxic shipping incident. It identifies staffing and ICT as recurring major problems and includes Radboudumc and Canisius-Wilhelmina participants.

Its flood case uses a dike breach near Bemmel and describes 1–4 metres over much of the area between Waal and Nederrijn within about 1.5 days. This official scenario concerns a specified north-of-Waal pathway and is not evidence of uniform depth across higher southern/eastern Nijmegen.

For flooding, staff residence/reachability, buffers, chain responsibilities/capacities, access and responder reach are explicitly unclear; hospitals may receive evacuees and distribute them across neighbouring regions.

For power, home medical-device batteries may last only hours, emergency diesel assumptions require verification and ambulance cycles/diversion grow. For ICT, mobile overload and one-to-three-day repair are scenario assumptions; emergency phones and analogue workarounds are not always tested.

For contaminated water, hospital tanker connections exist but not all are tested and supplier emergency capacity/timing is unclear. These Unknowns contradict exact unqualified Facilities, Water and Telecom recovery percentages.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / PDOK, ProRail, OVapi and RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Static road, crossing, rail, transit and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-light 2026-08-01 and transport snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03, CC0; ProRail station/track snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03, CC0; OVapi schedule valid 2026-08-30 through 2026-12-12; RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 2026-07-03, CC0
supports: Six logical road-border links connect Beuningen by A73, Overbetuwe by A15, Heumen by A73, Berg en Dal by N325 and Wijchen by N326/N324. They are boundary-derived logical edges, not independent real capacity or proof of current access.

The two A73 series entries use different physicalCorridorId values (NWB-road-783--A73 and NWB-road-73), while N326 lacks one. Crossings at the Waal/Spiegelwaal and Maas-Waalkanaal are not explicit failure or closure objects.

Five ProRail stations—Nijmegen, Dukenburg, Heyendaal, Goffert and Lent—and 273 GTFS stop areas are static/scheduled context. Geometry and timetables do not establish rolling-stock, bridge, power, crowding, closure, detour or emergency throughput.

RIVM's annual questionnaire identifies Radboudumc and Canisius-Wilhelmina as 24/7 emergency departments with acute obstetrics, respectively 22/19 rooms and 16,000/25,919 visits in 2025. It is not live capacity, staffing, backup, diversion or acceptance.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards and Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Partial water-control register, current observations and Waal forecast points
evidenceSources.edition: HWH snapshot retrieved 2026-09-03T01:38:15Z, CC BY-SA 4.0 with variable contributor completeness; Waterinfo observations retrieved 2026-09-02T18:03:18Z, generally ten-minute cadence; forecasts retrieved 2026-09-03T04:29:19Z; Waterinfo CC0 unless component-specific exception
supports: Full-resolution containment assigns sixty HWH points to GM0268: forty-six weirs, eight surface-water pumps, four sewer pumps and two sluices. Only six pump capacity fields are non-null; capacity units, catchments, connectivity, control and power/backup are not established.

Three duplicate Lent sewer-pump rows are labelled 'niet meer aanwezig' and must not count as operational. 'Gerealiseerd' on other registered objects denotes lifecycle/existence, not live availability during an incident.

Three local observations report Waal and Maas-Waalkanaal point levels at 2026-09-02T17:10–17:30Z. Four Waal forecast points provide T+1/+6/+12/+24 values of 476/478/478/477 cm NAP and are classified 'Verlaagde waterstand'.

The public forecast returned no Nijmegen point at T+48 or T+72. Point measurements/forecasts are not municipal inundation depth, defence state, threshold exceedance, canal propagation, pluvial surface or an instruction; Waterinfo is not mission-critical.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting, Netbeheer Nederland, RDI, DUO and RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Utility responsibilities, planning samples, facility registers and environmental observations
evidenceSources.edition: Public provider queries and deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; licence/cadence source-specific; NBNL sample is planning evidence rather than telemetry
supports: A point query yields overlapping Enexis/Liander electricity and Enexis/Liander/Stedin gas candidate polygons, Vitens drinking-water coverage, no drainage polygon and nine media candidates. Overlap or no-match is responsibility/context uncertainty, not multiple supply, service absence or connectivity.

One Nijmegen postcode sample (6543TX) maps to Liander area OS Winselingseweg 10-1i and publishes planning values, queues, 27 projects and an earliest 2030 date. It is neither municipal total nor current load, reserve, outage, switching or restoration.
RDI assigns 239 sites/505 antennas and DUO 129 education locations. Registers do not establish radio/telecom coverage, backhaul, power/backup, occupancy, shelter designation, supplies or staffing.

Two indicative RIVM stations reported PM2.5 and other pollutants at 2026-09-02T17:00Z. The deployment assigns zero local fixed KNMI weather observations, government-service points, NDW situations and 365-day seismic origins; every empty match is scoped NoData, never normal conditions, open roads or safety.

identity.summary: GM0268, Nijmegen, Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Gelderland-Zuid agree across generated and official 2025 sources.

The municipality reference point lies inside the generalized 2025 geometry.
Administrative edition, asset lifecycle, timestamped observations/forecasts and synthetic scenario time remain separate.

geography.summary: Administrative geography is coherent, but Waal/Spiegelwaal, Maas-Waalkanaal, defence, elevation, drainage and wildfire mechanisms are absent from the consequence model.
notes: Use full-resolution geometry for evidence containment; generalized geometry and the reference point are overview controls only.
Lent/Waalsprong north of the Waal, Waalfront/buitendijkse areas and higher south/east Nijmegen do not share one direct flood-depth field.
River flood, groundwater, pluvial sewer/ditch overload, drought water supply and vegetation fire are different causal pathways.

demography.summary: Resident population reconciles within CBS rounding and deterministic allocation preserves the municipal control.
notes: Published neighbourhood population is 189,020, thirteen above the 189,007 control (+0.007%).
Reconciliation removes thirteen residents deterministically without changing source observations.
Resident data exclude workers, students, visitors, road/rail/waterway users, responders and dynamic hospital/shelter occupancy.

regionalDetail.summary: All forty-four neighbourhoods are retained, but partial statistics and source-blind hazard allocation limit operational use.
notes: Lent, Stadscentrum, Hatert and Biezen are the largest resident rows, but population size is not flood, heat, fire or outage exposure.
District heating and charging are null everywhere; other source fields have one to four null rows and remain NoData.
Official flood, drainage and defence geometry does not drive neighbourhood depth or ordering.

settlements.summary: Lent and Nijmegen place/settlement context is internally coherent without inventing emergency roles.
notes: Both BAG place centres lie inside the generalized municipality boundary.
Both BRT features are woonkernen and do not duplicate population controls.
A station, school, hospital or named settlement is not automatically a shelter, support point, logistics hub or confirmed destination.

transport.summary: Static road/rail/transit context is traceable, but common-cause crossings, corridor identity, live route state and destination acceptance are unresolved.
notes: Six logical road edges connect five neighbours but do not represent Waal/Spiegelwaal or Maas-Waalkanaal crossing state, direction, detour or evacuation throughput.
A73's two series edges have inconsistent physical IDs and N326 has none; no nominal edge value may be summed or interpreted as vehicles/hour.
Five rail stations and 273 stop areas are location/schedule context, not confirmed incident-time service.

emergencyContext.summary: Authorities define credible local/regional hazards and care actions, but no selected GM0268 incident or complete T0–T+72 operational state exists.
notes: The Bemmel breach case is an official regional scenario, not a selected current incident and not a uniform Nijmegen surface.
Temporary pumps, dike works and hospital contingencies are dated action/planning records, not generic proof of availability or completion.
Support sites, shelters, staff, vehicles, fuel, generators, water stocks, care acceptance, route clearance and restoration remain Unknown where unpublished.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, resident/demand/delivery reconciliation, deterministic arithmetic and cumulative-burden invariants hold.

Neighbourhood population reconciles exactly to the municipality and service demand/delivery sums reconcile at every tested frame.
Cumulative deprived person-hours are non-decreasing, but numerical validity does not make their local cause or magnitude observed.

spatialPlausibility.summary: A common seeded forty-four-neighbourhood surface replaces Nijmegen's mechanism-specific water, terrain, fire, wind, heat, cyber and smoke geography.
notes: Nine active preset/component families reuse one local hazard-seed ordering rather than their own evidence-backed footprint.
River depth is applied broadly across north-bank, buitendijkse, low urban and higher eastern/southern areas without a selected defence failure or hydraulic result.
Moving wildfire ignition into Kwakkenberg produces 378 affected there but 3,790 in Lent; the containing neighbourhood ranks thirty-sixth by absolute affected population.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service availability omits Waal/canal controls, crossing dependencies, provider topology, hospital routes and operator state.

Provider polygons, one planning sample, antenna/school registers and annual hospital records do not calibrate live availability, occupancy, backup or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Arithmetic contribution ledgers reconcile, but public evidence and action provenance do not support the displayed local precision.
notes: Hazard/service contribution sums and counterfactual records remain inspectable.
At T+24 river output reports depth 3.300457, 84,443 affected residents and 1,927,869 person-hours; this is deterministic scenario arithmetic, not an authority observation or forecast.

The Groningen earthquake has zero local ground motion, severity and affected residents but still accumulates 51,768 person-hours at T+24 and 94,262 at T+72; any burden is indirect synthetic network scope, not local shaking damage.

recovery72h.summary: T+72 plateaus, deterioration and recovery are not driven by a confirmed Nijmegen action/resource ledger or an official T+72 Waal forecast.
notes: River depth stays 3.300457 while affected residents rise 84,443→91,643 and burden 1,927,869→7,388,603 from T+24 to T+72; Facilities falls 0.659990→0.466875 without a selected access, evacuation, staffing or relief action.
Compound depth changes only 0.365004→0.354951 while affected residents rise 92,988→95,391 and burden 2,020,816→7,636,791; service plateaus lack accountable actions or resources.

The public Nijmegen Waal forecast stops at T+24. No inspected record confirms T+72 pump/barrier state, bridge access, hospital acceptance, generator/fuel, water distribution, shelter, resupply or restoration completion.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, centre containment, regional membership and resident reconciliation are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 plus audit:context verify GM0268/Nijmegen/Gelderland/VRGZ, the contained reference point and a thirteen-resident (+0.007%) neighbourhood rounding difference reconciled deterministically.
findings.action: Retain the 2025 source edition, exact official nulls, deterministic reconciliation and separate BAG/BRT semantics.

findings.summary: Nine active hazard/component families reuse one source-blind forty-four-neighbourhood surface.
findings.evidence: Diagnostics/model inspection show one common scenario seed and neighbourhood-ID hash drive local severity regardless of river/terrain, rainfall/drainage, wind, heat, cyber origin or smoke plume; controlled Kwakkenberg ignition does not privilege the containing neighbourhood.
findings.action: Suppress local consequence maps until each mechanism samples a governed event footprint; test source containment, hydraulic/terrain/fuel geometry and cross-hazard rank divergence.

findings.summary: The uniform 3.300457 river depth contradicts Nijmegen's selected-pathway requirement and available Waal forecast scope.
findings.evidence: At T+24/T+72 the model holds depth 3.300457 while affected residents rise 84,443→91,643. E03/E05 distinguish Waalfront, Lent/Bemmel and higher city geography; E07 provides Waal point forecasts only through T+24, not inundation or defence failure.
findings.action: Require a selected LIWO/authority hydraulic event with breach/overflow location, boundary/datum, defence/control state, AHN footprint, arrival/recession, uncertainty and licence; otherwise direct local depth, affected and service consequence remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Pluvial output is not bound to Nijmegen's terrain, groundwater, sewer, gully, ditch or receiving-water mechanisms.
findings.evidence: At T+24 rainfall is zero while depth is 0.351353, affected residents 12,333 and burden 730,923. E02 distinguishes multiple local pathways and known western groundwater nuisance; E07 supplies partial assets but no connected valid-time system state.
findings.action: Bind a versioned rainfall event to AHN/BGT flow, municipal stress-test geometry, GWSW/sewer/gully/ditch/canal topology, storage, controls, blockage, power and recession; render missing fields Unknown.

findings.summary: Controlled Kwakkenberg ignition fails source containment and yields population-weighted remote consequences.
findings.evidence: A controlled T+24 ignition at [5.891681436928109,51.82746099630658] creates city fire 0.513013, smoke 0.566285 and 47,436 affected; Kwakkenberg has 378 affected and ranks 36th, while Lent has 3,790 and ranks first. The canonical remote ignition produces smoke without an observed plume.
findings.action: Require eligible fuel, ignition time/location, moisture, wind/plume, barriers/access and suppression state; assert containing/adjacent fuel exposure before unrelated population and label remote smoke synthetic until a valid forecast/observation is bound.

findings.summary: Partial water assets and point measurements are visible but cannot support exact Water/Drainage performance.
findings.evidence: E07 contains sixty points, only six non-null pump capacities and three local observations. Three duplicate Lent sewer-pump records explicitly say 'niet meer aanwezig'; other lifecycle labels, capacity numbers and water levels do not establish connected operability, remaining capacity or restoration.
findings.action: Exclude removed records from operational counts; integrate authority-approved GWSW/water-board topology and unit-compatible valid-time aggregate state where publishable, otherwise preserve affectsSimulation=false and Unknown performance.

findings.summary: Corridor aliases and missing crossing objects hide Waal/canal common-cause access failures.
findings.evidence: E06 shows two A73 series edges with inconsistent physicalCorridorIds, a missing N326 corridor ID and no explicit Waal/Spiegelwaal or Maas-Waalkanaal crossing state. Five rail stations and 273 stops do not prove live incident throughput.
findings.action: Canonicalize A73/N326 identities, model Waal and canal crossings once as shared physical assets, and gate road/rail/bus, care, supply and evacuation workflows on direction-specific valid-time operator/NDW state or explicit synthetic assumptions.

findings.summary: Exact Facilities availability contradicts documented unknown staff, access, buffer and acceptance state.
findings.evidence: River Facilities falls 0.659990→0.466875 from T+24 to T+72 and compound changes 0.494386→0.454948. E05 explicitly leaves staff reachability, responder access, buffers, chain responsibilities/capacity and several emergency arrangements unclear; E06 is annual hospital context only.
findings.action: Represent Radboudumc/CWZ and alternatives as time-valid origin-route-destination workflows; retain staffing, occupancy, diversion/acceptance, backup, supplies and restoration as Unknown unless confirmed by responsible authorities.

findings.summary: Provider areas, planning queues and facility registers cannot calibrate exact utility availability.
findings.evidence: E08 returns overlapping electricity/gas/media candidates, no drainage provider feature, one Liander planning sample, 239 antenna sites and 129 education locations but no physical connectivity, live load/flow/quality/outage, backhaul, backup, staff, stock or repair state.
findings.action: Label percentages synthetic; ingest only authorised timestamped aggregate outage/restoration data, preserve topology/security limits, and never convert overlap, no-match or one sample into municipal coverage or zero.

findings.summary: Observation and forecast layers need strict location, time, horizon, quality and coverage semantics.
findings.evidence: E07 has three water observations and four Waal forecasts through T+24; E08 has two indicative air stations but zero fixed KNMI observations, government points, NDW situations and recent seismic origins. No T+48/T+72 Waal match is present.
findings.action: Display source, issue/valid time, units, datum, quality, point footprint and horizon; prohibit silent interpolation/projection and render absent coverage NoData rather than normal water/weather, clean air, open roads or safety.

findings.summary: Correct narrow direct zeros and indirect effects require explicit scope labels.
findings.evidence: Direct coastal depth and Groningen-earthquake ground motion are zero, while coastal wind/service burden and earthquake person-hours persist from synthetic wider-network effects; canonical wildfire is remote smoke. None is local coastal inundation, shaking damage or an observed plume.
findings.action: Retain supported direct zeros only within the named component/source scope, label indirect network/smoke effects separately and never infer all-hazard safety.

findings.summary: First-72-hour deterioration and recovery lack accountable actions, resources and a valid T+72 hydraulic boundary.
findings.evidence: River and compound affected/service/burden trajectories change through T+72 although E07 stops Nijmegen Waal forecasts at T+24 and E05 documents unresolved care/logistics constraints. No source confirms barrier/pump switching, crossing clearance, hospital acceptance, shelter, fuel, generators, water distribution, resupply or restoration.
findings.action: Add a timestamped T0–6–12–24–48–72 incident/action/resource/blocker ledger; suppress recovery attribution and operational site/count claims when authority state or forecast horizon is absent.

corrections.summary: Replace GM0268's generic river/pluvial fields with selected Waal/Spiegelwaal/defence and rain–terrain–drainage events while retaining narrow direct-coastal zero.
corrections.validation: Assert source event, breach/overflow or pluvial pathway, boundary/datum, defence/control state, AHN footprint, issue/valid time, arrival/recession, uncertainty/licence and NoData; forecast points stop at their published horizon and unsupported depth/affected/service/recovery is Unknown.

corrections.summary: Replace the shared local seed with mechanism-specific footprints and enforce Kwakkenberg wildfire source containment.
corrections.validation: Water, wind, heat, smoke and cyber use distinct evidence-backed surfaces; a controlled eligible Kwakkenberg ignition affects its containing/adjacent fuel region before unrelated Lent and cross-service physical hazard remains invariant.

corrections.summary: Govern Nijmegen's water-control/sewer chain without converting partial registers or point observations into live/future performance.
corrections.validation: Removed Lent records cannot count operationally; source/version/licence/coverage, lifecycle and capacity nulls persist; only connected unit-compatible valid-time barrier/gate/pump/sewer/control/backup state affects services.

corrections.summary: Represent Waal/Spiegelwaal and Maas-Waalkanaal crossings, A73/N326 corridor identity, rail/transit and acute-care access as non-additive time-valid workflows.
corrections.validation: A73 series edges never add capacity; corridor IDs are canonical; crossing closure propagates once to eligible road/rail/bus, Mobility/Supply and care routes; live state and hospital acceptance remain Unknown when absent.

corrections.summary: Make first-72-hour service and recovery changes depend on confirmed or visibly synthetic actions, resources and blockers.
corrections.validation: Every T0/6/12/24/48/72 change cites incident, actor, action, resource, valid time and constraint; absent staff, support sites, fuel, shelter, care acceptance, water distribution, route clearance or restoration is Unknown.

residualLimitations: No inspected public source supplies complete safe-to-publish Liander/Enexis/Stedin/Vitens/telecom/sewer/water-control topology, current state, backup endurance, priority users, crews or restoration estimates.
No governed public catalogue supplies Nijmegen emergency-support locations with live opening, staff, stocks, fuel, shelter capacity, care acceptance or completed first-72-hour actions.
HWH aggregation is partial, most capacities are null and three Lent sewer-pump records are explicitly absent; registered existence is not incident-time operability.
Waalfront, Sprok–Sterreschans–Heteren, Spiegelwaal and temporary Waalsprong pump records are project/dynamic context, not a universal protection guarantee or generic scenario state.
Three Waterinfo observations, four forecasts through T+24 and two indicative air stations retain point/time validity only; sparse or empty matches are scoped NoData.
Dynamic workers, students, visitors, road/rail/waterway users, hospital/shelter occupants and responders are absent from resident exposure.
NWB nominal capacities are generalized scenario units; no conclusion about real bridge, junction, crossing, evacuation or supply throughput is supported.
Exact local hazard, affected, service, person-hour and recovery values remain synthetic until an authority-reviewed event and operational action ledger are bound.
provinceReviewFlags: Coordinate one Waal flood scenario family across Nijmegen, Overbetuwe, Lingewaard, Berg en Dal and Beuningen; do not tune municipality-wide depths independently of breach/overflow selection, defences, Spiegelwaal, AHN and arrival/recession.
Review Lent/Waalsprong, Sprok–Sterreschans, Waalfront/Honig, the south/east high terrain and Maas-Waalkanaal/Sluis Weurt as distinct pathways and operational zones.
Audit Waal/Spiegelwaal and Maas-Waalkanaal bridge, rail, bus, evacuation, responder, hospital and supply dependencies once as shared cross-boundary physical assets.
Canonicalize A73 and N326 physical-corridor identities across Gelderland/Brabant neighbours; series boundary links are never independent capacity.
Coordinate Radboudumc, CWZ and alternative regional/cross-region acute-care origin-route-destination capacity using VRGZ's documented Unknown staff, access, buffers and acceptance semantics.

Require Gelderland-wide NoData rules for Waterinfo horizon gaps, sparse KNMI/RIVM/RWS/NDW observations, provider overlaps and partial HWH registers; nearest/empty coverage is never a municipality value or all-clear.
Review the shared seeded neighbourhood surface and unsupported T+72 action/recovery assumptions as national model issues rather than accepting Nijmegen-specific calibration.
